{{DISPLAYTITLE:''q''-expansion principle}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''''q''-expansion principle''' states that a [[modular form]] ''f'' has coefficients in a [[module (mathematics)|module]] ''M'' if its ''q''-expansion at enough [[Cusp (singularity)|cusp]]s resembles the ''q''-expansion of a modular form ''g'' with coefficients in ''M''. It was introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Katz|year=1973|authorlink=Nicholas Katz|loc=corollaries 1.6.2, 1.12.2}}.
